entities.summary:
Illumination, an American animation film production company founded in 2007, is headquartered in Santa Monica, California, and has made significant contributions to the global animation landscape. The firm emerged during a transformative period marked by a resurgence in animated features, fueled by advancements in digital technology and changing audience demographics, particularly among children and young adults. Key figures in its establishment include directors and animators who sought to innovate storytelling techniques and visual aesthetics within the genre, thereby expanding the boundaries of animated cinema.

The company quickly gained recognition for its work on films such as "Despicable Me," which premiered in 2010 and became a cultural phenomenon, grossing over $500 million worldwide. Illumination's approach to animation blends humor with heartfelt narratives, appealing to diverse audiences and setting new benchmarks for success in animated films. Its use of cutting-edge animation technology and a focus on character-driven stories have allowed it to produce several blockbuster franchises, including the "Minions" series, which further solidified its status in the industry.

Illumination's legacy is marked by its influence on the animation industry, prompting other studios to adopt similar styles and storytelling approaches. Its films have not only entertained millions but also generated substantial revenue, contributing to the growth of the global animation market, which was valued at approximately $270 billion in 2021. The company's success has inspired a new generation of animators and filmmakers, illustrating the power of animated storytelling in contemporary culture.
